claims.text: When an Output<T> is treated as a plain value (e.g., string-converted), Pulumi produces placeholder text such as 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' in log lines, generated files, or resource properties instead of the actual value.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and describes this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an Output value, branching on it, or reading it like a plain value produces errors.
Pulumi Cloud returns a '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' error when another update is in progress on the stack.

Pulumi Cloud console lets you recover a recently deleted stack, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
The debugging/logging page covers automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide has an anchor #automatic-logging covering the `pulumi logs share` command.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com offering community support.

Pulumi offers paid support options via the contact page.
The update conflict content was moved to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/, and the #conflict hash redirects there (tracked at pulumi/pulumi issue 20846).
The verbose logging content lives at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, and the #verbose-logging hash redirects there (tracked at pulumi/docs issue 16985).
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.

When an output value is converted to a string directly (concatenated or logged) instead of via apply or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.

In Python, using an Output in an f-string produces a broken string containing text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning without raising an exception.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the way to serialize an Output to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.

In C#, converting an Output to a string via interpolation silently produces a string containing text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes the output-to-string mistake throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.
When converting an output to a string by mistake, the program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds, with the placeholder text surfacing later.

The string-composition helpers for outputs are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
The page links to /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ for examples of using apply and multiple outputs.
A value read from an output inside an apply callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it).
The apply callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading the outer variable.
An Output can be passed directly as the input to a resource (e.g. `aws.s3.BucketObject` `bucket`) without apply, and Pulumi resolves the dependency.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, but a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output evaluates the output object itself, which is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
Branching that depends on a resource's output must be moved inside `apply`, expressing both outcomes as values (e.g. `vpc.vpcId.apply(id => id.startsWith("vpc-0") ? 3 : 6)`).
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts depend on data only known after a resource is created, one fix is to provision dependent resources in a separate later stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
The page links to /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences for StackReference.
Trying to `await` an output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
The page links to /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ for the Automation API.
